newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech SocDems attack IPB bank sale plan.
newsitem.headline: Czech SocDems attack IPB bank sale plan.

text.p: The opposition Czech Social Democrats criticised on Friday the centre-right government's plan to sell its stake in bank IPB a.s., but said they did not oppose bank privatisation outright.

The party's spokesman for financial issues Ivo Svoboda said the party did not oppose privatisation of state holdings in the "Big Four" Czech banks, but added that it should be done only after the capital market was cleaned up.
Widespread cross-ownership of banks, their investment funds and industrial companies should be resolved before the state stakes were sold, he told a news conference.
"(The IPB plan) means that the government has absolutely no concept. Privatisation must be built on a long-term concept which will say what is the aim of privatisation," he said.
"The influence of banks goes significantly beyond the loans they have provided," he said, noting that they held stakes in many industrial companies through their investment arms.

The Social Democrats have gained strong influence in parliament since the coalition of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus lost is majority in June. But the government can privatise the banks by executive order without parliamentary approval.

The Czech state still holds 48.9 percent in commercial bank Komercni Banka a.s., 66 percent in trade bank Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s., 45 percent in savings bank Ceska Sporitelna a.s. and 31.5 percent in IPB.
The Big Four control some 80 percent of the credit market.
On Wednesday, the cabinet charged Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik with drawing up criteria for choosing a foreign partner for IPB as soon as possible.

Svoboda said the Social Democrats believed the state stakes could become assets of one or more pension funds which could partially substitute the current pension insurance system, under which contributions are directly redistributed among pensioners.

If there were no consensus with the coalition led by Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) on how to reshape the banking sector, the Social Democrats would start to do so according to their own plans once they gained power, he said.
"Then it will be necessary to adopt systematic measures to untie the deeply-tied ownership (of banks and industry)," Svoboda said.
The Czech capital market has been often criticised for a lack of transparency, and some analysts say that the banks' supremacy over the industrial sector is harming the economy.
